summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the colon and CNS, status post bowel resection and colostomy, was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting over 10 days, with recent deterioration. Imaging revealed a dilated segment of small bowel near a jejunojejunal anastomosis with fecalized material and new wall thickening, suggestive of a functional small bowel obstruction. Infectious causes were ruled out by negative stool studies. She improved clinically with supportive care and antibiotics, which were discontinued due to lack of infection signs. Surgical intervention was not required. The obstruction resolved, and she tolerated a diet advance. She was discharged home with plans for outpatient magnetic resonance enterography to evaluate bowel function, while continuing management of chronic conditions including DLBCL in remission, common variable immunodeficiency, diabetes, and chronic pain.
